v)              
Partnerships with voluntary sector and other not-for-profit
organisations (e.g. IW Community Action).
 
 
vi)            
Collaborations with health and social care partners towards

vii)

Following the
completion of the external audit process, consideration was given
to the report which sought approval for the Statement of Accounts
for 2024-25.
 
Concerns were raised
that the report “options” section restricted the range
of choices, noting that approval was contingent on the committee
being satisfied with the accounts. Reference was made to the
professional responsibilities of the Section 151 Officer, and it
was emphasised that while the committee could theoretically choose
not to approve the accounts, such a decision would require clear,
substantive justification.
 
It was assured that
the council’s position was not atypical among local
authorities nationally, and that the Finance department had taken
steps to address the previous capacity issues going forward.
Committee members acknowledged the external commentary regarding
the implications of not approving the accounts and recognised that
the government expected historic accounts to be completed by the
statutory deadline.
 
Given the progress
made and the assurances received, it was cautioned that any refusal
to approve the accounts would not be appropriate as the backlog was
known and expected. The chair raised concerns about signing the
accounts without being able to formally record an explanation
alongside the signature. Committee members were advised that
councillors acting in good faith were protected from personal
liability.
 
It was agreed that
the minutes should reflect that the committee had considered the
Statement of Accounts, noted the concerns raised by the external
auditors in their external audit results report, and reviewed the
timeline for improvements. Following a vote, it was:
 
RESOLVED:
 
THAT the 2024-25
Statement of Accounts, including the Annual Governance Statement,
be approved and duly signed by the person presiding at the
meeting.

content:
Pharmacy Services
 
Consideration was given to the report of the
NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight Integrated Care Board (ICB), which
provided an update and overview on pharmacy services on the Isle of
Wight including statistics on pharmacy first, the use of pharmacies
generally and the increasing use of online pharmacies for a growing
age range.
 
The committee were advised of a pharmacy
closure in Ventnor earlier that day which had taken effect from the
previous day, this had been regrettable however necessary, it was a
fast moving situation and contingencies had been put in place to
ensure provision for residents in the area who relied on the
service provided were sufficient. Issues relating to other
pharmacies run by the same company were ongoing and the ICB were
working with NHS England to manage the situation, details would be
provided as soon as possible.
 
Councillor K Love understood the situation and
raised concerns regarding the loss of the pharmacy first service
which had been undertaken in pharmacies and asked what
communication was being put out for residents in areas affected. He
was advised that other local pharmacies had taken on additional
work to help the situation. This issue had been discussed at high
level in government so was being closely monitored. GPs had
assisted and continued to provide patients with advice on where to
collect prescriptions.
 
There was concern regarding private flu
vaccinations and the increasing length of time people had to wait,
advice was that more capacity was opening, and they were looking at
opening more areas for vaccinations to keep up with demand.
 
Questions were asked regarding online
prescription medications and how this was being regulated and
supervised, it was noted that concerns had been raised and there
had been more regulations in recent years, they were advised to
report through the ICB who would pass on the information.
 
A reduction in available prescription drugs
was discussed and it was explained that in some instances this was
a national issue however where an alternative was available the
pharmacist should be able to make a change.
 
Dentistry
 
Consideration was given to the report of the
NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight Integrated Care Board (ICB), which
provided an update and overview of dentistry and dental services on
the Isle of Wight, including the challenges, the current national
contract, and the steps taken to work with providers and to improve
access to NHS dental care.
 
It was acknowledged that there had been an
increase in the number of dental visits on the Island, a new centre
had been commissioned which would achieve a 48% increase in the
number of units of dental activity. Existing dentists had helped
along with a strong partnership with Public Health.
A push to encourage young people to become
dentists was being undertaken.
 
Questions were asked regarding the number of
trained Ukrainian dentists whose qualifications had not been
recognised in the UK who may be able to assist with the lack of
dentists. It would be taken back, and an answer would be provide to
the Committee.
 
It was noted that Looked After Children
currently do not have access to a dedicated dentist, which was
considered essential. The committee was informed that there is a
significant waiting list, and that additional resources are
required due to a shortage in dental service provision.
 
ICB Update
It was noted that regular meetings were taking
place with the Hospice, including talking about whole system
provider which had been evidenced by hospices across the UK, an
update would be provided to Healthwatch before the end of 2025.
 
RESOLVED:
 
THAT the updates be noted

The Committee asked if targets could be
introduced to show the direction of movement and understand the
level of resources required for the service, in response the
Director of Adult Social Care advised that the department was a
demand driven service and meeting the needs of vulnerable residents
was the priority.
 
Questions were asked regarding the home finder
process and the number of people accessing the service, the
Director for Adult Social Care advised that some people did not
meet the criteria for Home Finder, voluntary sector partners
provided a good service to assist in filling the gap in providing
housing advice.

THAT the operational and financial performance
of the Adult Social Care and Housing Needs and Public Health
directorates be noted.

decision_maker: Adult Social Care, Public Health and Housing Needs Committee
content:
The Committee received a comprehensive
presentation which outlined the arrangements between Inclusion
Recovery Isle of Wight, the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare
NHS Foundation Trust, and partners including Public Health, to
develop joint care pathways to meet service users’ mental
health and drug and/or alcohol needs.
 
The committee asked if there was work that
could be achieved at local level to identify and help with the
prevention of these addictions, the Director of Public Health
advised that the earliest intervention was key and the 1001 first
day’s programme was a critical element to try to break
cycles. It was noted that stress, trauma, poverty, poor housing and
employment were also key triggers.
 
It was noted that an increase in numbers could
be seen as a success to the number of people accessing the services
available, as GP’s provided support and signposted people to
the services provided.
 
A fifth pathway was evolving looking at life
histories and identifying where intervention could have helped turn
the situation around for people. The Committee suggested that
secondary school children had been missed, they were advised that
the inclusion team worked closely with schools and childhood
experiences was a wider children’s agenda.
 
The Director for Adult Social Care advised
that commissioning was underway for a new area, and they were
exploring the opportunity for a dry house on the Isle of Wight.
 
The committee asked what the goal was going
forward, the Director for Public Health advised that targets were
important, and some were linked to commissioning targets.
 
RESOLVED:
 
THAT the presentation be noted.
topline: The Adult Social Care, Public Health and Housing Needs Committee has decided to develop joint care pathways to meet service users' mental health and drug/alcohol needs

content:
The Strategic Director for Children’s
Services provided the committee with an update of current
highlights and challenges within the directorate.
 
Highlights included:
 
·      
A focus on earlier needs identification of families
to prevent escalation in order to reduce
the number of Education and Health Care Plans (EHCPs), Child
Protection Plans (CPPs) and children in care.
·      
A focus across the directorate to improve school
attendance.
·      
The continued progress on Corporate Parenting
work.
·      
People across the directorate, council and wider
community working well together.
 
The highlighted challenges were:
 
·      
The needs of children and families remained high.
There was still a high number of requests for EHCPs and the number
of CPPs remained high.
·      
These numbers would not change
and reduce soon due to a number of
factors including cost of living, unstable housing, adult mental
health, substance misuse, and domestic abuse.
·      
Homes for children.
·      
Financial overspend due to home
to school transport, agency social workers and the cost of
providing homes for children.
 
The
committee had a further discussion about the importance of adult
learning in supporting vulnerable parents and improving aspirations
for themselves and their children. It was shared that a paper on
adult learning would come to the next committee meeting.
 
The
Service Director for Children’s Social Care provided a brief
update to the committee on the government’s Social Care
Reforms. It was agreed that a paper would be brought to a future
meeting.
 
RESOLVED
 
i)                
THAT the Committee note the operational and
financial performance of the Children’s Services
Directorate.

 
ii)              
THAT the Committee agree the current Directorate priorities and
 
iii)             
THAT the Committee delegate authority to the Director of
Children’s Services to draft the relevant section of a
revised corporate plan.
topline: The Children's Services, Education and Skills Committee has decided to approve recommendations to address the high needs of children and families, improve school attendance, and delegate authority for drafting a section of a revised corporate plan.

content:
The Home to School Transport Project Officer
presented the report to the committee. The policy was previously
agreed in 2024, but it was recognised that certain areas needed to
be reviewed and amended and a consultation on these changes was
required.
 
RESOLVED
 
THAT the
Committee approve proceeding with a public consultation on
the proposed changes to the School Transport Policy and Post 16
Transport Statement with a further report setting out the findings
of the consultation to be presented at a future Committee early in
2026.
topline: The Children's Services, Education and Skills Committee has decided to review and amend the School Transport Policy and Post 16 Transport Statement.

content:
The Strategic Manager for People and
Organisational Development shared the report which set out the
learning and development activities recommended for members of the
committee.
 
The committee discussed the plan and agreed
that training undertaken by members should be published. It was
agreed that members would complete the initial training by January
and an updated plan would be presented to the committee.
 
RESOLVED
 
i)                
THAT the Committee approves the content of the report and begins to
undertake the learning and development required of them. Any new
learning to be added to the committee requirements should be
discussed and agreed by committee members.
 
ii)              
THAT Committee members agree to complete all required training, and
an updated report is brought to the January committee meeting.
topline: The Committee has decided to approve recommendations for learning and development activities for its members.

content:
It was explained that this report was
requested in June and was about going back to basics with the
School Place Planning process. It was acknowledged that the
situation facing schools was now critical and although no one
wanted to close schools, it needed to be addressed urgently.
 
The feedback from recent events held with
heads and governing bodies was shared as well as a response from
the DfE’s Regional Director for the South
East. Representatives from the Church of England and
Catholic dioceses were present virtually and spoke.
 
The Service Director for Education Access and
Inclusion highlighted each of the possible options and noted that
each option had strengths and weaknesses.
 
Further discussion took place around place
planning areas, the importance of using clear criteria and the
communication of this, any potential impact of the proposed
devolution, and proposed timelines.
 
RESOLVED
 
THAT the
Committee approves commencement of a:
 
i)           
period of engagement with stakeholders to
establish:
i.            
the key principles of the future structure of the
school system on the Isle of Wight.
ii.           
the options available to move to such a structure
within an appropriate timescale.
 
ii)          
consultation on the school place planning
areas.
 
iii)        
review of the School Place Planning
Strategy.
topline: The UK council has decided to approve recommendations for the future structure of the school system on the Isle of Wight and the school place planning process.

content:
The Leader introduced the report and advised
that following government decision to allow the Isle of Wight to be
part of the Devolution priority programme this is a need to
formally consent to government laying the parliamentary order.
 
Alterations to the recommendations had been
circulated around the room.  Firstly, it
was proposed that the recommendations be taken as one vote.
 
Secondly, to alter recommendation 8 to read as
follows:
 
8.              
That Full Council gives delegated authority to the
Chief Executive after consultation with Cllrs Jordan, Blake,
Garratt, Jarman and Gladwin to agree the final form of any draft
Parliamentary Order (Statutory Instrument) that the Government
wishes to lay before Parliament to create a new Mayoral County
Combined Authority (MCCA).
 
The alteration was put and duly seconded, in
line with the constitution (Part 4 – paragraph 4.125) a vote
was taken the result of which was:
 
RESOLVED:
 
THAT the alterations were accepted
 
Cllr P Spink advised that he had raised
a number of procedural concerns with the
Monitoring Officer relating to the item under discussion at this
meeting, he asked that it be noted that he did not consider the
advice received in response to be correct, however noted that he
was bound by the advice provided.
 
Concern was raised regarding the content of
the Mayoral Development Orders in particular the Local Planning
Authority process and the ability of a Mayor to call in planning decisions.
 
Ferries had not been included as part of the
functions of the Mayoral County Combined Authority (MCCA) however
it was noted that this could be added once the MCCA was
established.
 
The meeting adjourned and reconvened.
 
A vote was taken the result of which was:
 
RESOLVED
 





6.              
That Full Council notes the summary of the draft
Statutory Instrument set out in Appendix 1 and approves in
principle the establishment of the Hampshire and Solent Mayoral
Combined County Authority (consent to the Statutory
Instrument).

 
7.              
That Full Council notes the summary of the powers
and competencies (functions) in the English Devolution and
Community Empowerment Bill as set out in Appendix 2.

 
8.              
That Full Council gives delegated authority to the
Chief Executive after consultation with Cllrs Jordan, Blake,
Garratt, Jarman and Gladwin to agree the final form of any draft
Parliamentary Order (Statutory Instrument) that the Government
wishes to lay before Parliament to create a new Mayoral County
Combined Authority (MCCA).
 
9.              
Resolve that Natalie Brahma-Pearl, Returning Officer
and Chief Executive at Portsmouth City Council, is to be appointed
as the Combined County Authority Returning Officer (CCARO) for the
2026 mayoral elections as outlined in the report.
topline: The Full Council has decided to approve the establishment of the Hampshire and Solent Mayoral Combined County Authority.
